questions.question: The Hindi novel 'Jhutha Sach' is written by:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Yashpal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yashpal** is a renowned Hindi writer and is considered one of the most important figures in modern Hindi literature.
 
• He was born on **December 3, 1903, in Firozpur, Punjab**, India, and passed away on **December 26, 1976**.
 
• **'Jhutha Sach'** (translated as "The False Truth") is regarded as Yashpal's magnum opus and one of the most celebrated novels in Hindi literature.
 
• The novel, published in two parts—**'Vatan Aur Desh'** and **'Desh Ka Bhavishya'**—explores the social, political, and emotional upheavals during and after the **Partition of India in 1947**.
 
• The book is known for its **realistic portrayal of the struggles** of common people, their relationships, and the impact of the partition on their lives.
 
• Yashpal was also a freedom fighter and a revolutionary, and his works often reflect his **progressive and socialist ideologies**.
 
• In 1970, Yashpal was awarded the **Sahitya Akademi Award** for his novel **'Meri Teri Uski Baat'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jaishankar Prasad**__

 __
 
• **Jaishankar Prasad** was a prominent Hindi poet, novelist, and playwright.
 
• He is best known for his works in the **Chhayavad (Neo-romanticism) movement** in Hindi literature.
 
• His famous works include **'Kamayani'** (an epic poem), **'Skandagupta'** (a play), and **'Kankal'** (a novel).
 
• Prasad's writings often explore themes of **philosophy, spirituality, and patriotism**.
 
 
 
• **Shrilal Shukla**__
 __
 
• **Shrilal Shukla** is best known for his satirical novel **'Raag Darbari'**, which provides a critical view of post-independence rural India.
 
• He received the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in 1969 for **'Raag Darbari'**.
 
• His works often focus on **corruption and the socio-political dynamics** of Indian villages.
 
 
 
• **Premchand**__
 
 
• **Premchand**, born as **Dhanpat Rai Shrivastava**, is one of the most celebrated Hindi and Urdu writers in Indian literature.
 
• He is known as the **'Upanyas Samrat' (Emperor of Novels)**.
 
• His notable works include **'Godan'**, **'Gaban'**, **'Nirmala'**, and **'Karmabhoomi'**.
 
• Premchand's writings often reflect **social realism** and address issues like poverty, caste discrimination, and women's rights.

questions.question: 'Attolu Eidu' is the cultural festival of which of the following union territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Attolu Eidu'** is a cultural festival celebrated in the **Lakshadweep** Islands, an archipelago of 36 islands located in the **Arabian Sea.**
 
• The festival reflects the **traditional and cultural heritage** of the Lakshadweep community, which is predominantly **Muslim**.
 
• 'Attolu Eidu' is significant as it showcases the **rich traditions, folk music, and dance** unique to this region.
 
• Lakshadweep is known for its **peaceful way of life**, and the festival is an occasion for communal harmony and joy.
 
• The cultural festivities often include performances of **Kolkkali**, a traditional dance form, and other **local art forms**.
 
• The islands are governed as a **Union Territory of India**, and its population has a deep connection to the sea, which influences their festivals and livelihoods.
 
• Lakshadweep's festivals are an important part of its identity, promoting **tourism** and preserving the **islands' unique cultural heritage.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir**__

 __
 
• Jammu and Kashmir is a Union Territory in the northernmost part of India, known for its **Himalayan landscapes and rich cultural heritage.**
 
• It is famous for festivals like **Lohri, Eid-ul-Fitr, and Navroz,** but 'Attolu Eidu' is not celebrated here.
 
 
 
• **Dadra and Nagar Haveli**__
 __
 
• This Union Territory is located in western India and is known for its **tribal culture and festivals** like Tarpa Dance Festival, but it is unrelated to 'Attolu Eidu.'
 
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__
 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are known for their **Indigenous tribes and natural beauty**, but their cultural festivals are distinct and do not include 'Attolu Eidu.'

questions.question: According Census 2011 of India, which of the following union territories has the second highest literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Daman and Diu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census 2011 of India**, the **Union Territory** of **Daman and Diu** has the **second highest literacy rate** among the Union Territories.
 
• The literacy rate of **Daman and Diu** is recorded at **87.07%**, which places it just below Lakshadweep, the Union Territory with the highest literacy rate.
 
• **Daman and Diu** are located on the western coast of India and were a part of the Portuguese territories in India until 1961.
 
• The high literacy rate in this region can be attributed to efforts in promoting education and the availability of basic educational infrastructure.
 
• Post the **merger of Daman and Diu with Dadra and Nagar Haveli in January 2020**, they now form a single Union Territory.
 
• The Union Territory has a relatively small population, which has contributed to effective implementation of educational policies and initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lakshadweep**__

 __
 
• **Lakshadweep** has the **highest literacy rate** among the Union Territories as per the **Census 2011**, recorded at **91.85%**.
 
• The Union Territory consists of a group of **36 small islands** and is located in the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• The high literacy rate is due to the consistent educational efforts and literacy programs implemented by the government.
 
 
 
• **Chandigarh**__
 __
 
• Chandigarh, a Union Territory and the capital of both **Punjab and Haryana**, has a literacy rate of **86.05%**.
 
• The city is known for its planned urban infrastructure and strong emphasis on education.
 
• It houses several prestigious educational institutions, such as **Panjab University**.
 
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__
 
 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, located in the Bay of Bengal, have a literacy rate of **86.63%**.
 
• The geographical isolation and scattered islands present challenges in providing uniform educational access, but significant progress has been made in improving literacy.
 
• The islands are known for their rich biodiversity and indigenous tribal communities.

questions.question: Chand Minar at Daulatabad is a 210-feet-high tapering tower divided into _____ storeys.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chand Minar** is located at **Daulatabad Fort**, situated in the Indian state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• It is a **210-feet-high tapering tower**, making it one of the tallest towers in the country.
 
• The tower is divided into **four storeys**, each adorned with **decorative balconies**.
 
• It is constructed of **red sandstone** and is an excellent example of the blend of **Persian and Indian architectural styles**.
 
• The Chand Minar was built in the **15th century** by **Ala-ud-din Bahmani** to commemorate his conquest of the fort.
 
• It serves as a significant **historical monument** and showcases the **engineering brilliance** of the medieval period.
 
• The tower also had a functional purpose, serving as a **watchtower** and a symbol of victory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Daulatabad Fort**__

 __
 
• The **Daulatabad Fort** is located near **Aurangabad** in Maharashtra.
 
• It was originally known as **Devagiri**, meaning "Hill of Gods."
 
• The fort is known for its **defensive architecture**, including its **moats, steep slopes, and maze-like entry paths**.
 
• It was briefly the capital of the Delhi Sultanate under the rule of **Mohammed bin Tughlaq**.
 
 
 
• **Ala-ud-din Bahmani**__
 
 
• He was a ruler of the **Bahmani Sultanate**, which was based in the Deccan region of India.
 
• Ala-ud-din Bahmani is known for his contributions to **art and architecture** during his reign.
 
• The Chand Minar is one of his most famous architectural achievements.

questions.question: Which of the following is a natural indicator for acid and base?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**China rose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **China rose**, scientifically known as **Hibiscus rosa-sinensis**, is a natural indicator for acids and bases.
 
• It is widely used in experiments to determine the **pH** of substances.
 
• The petals of the flower exhibit a **color change** based on the pH of the solution it is exposed to:
 
• In an **acidic medium**, the color changes to **dark pink or magenta.**
 
• In a **basic medium**, the color changes to **greenish-yellow.**

 
• This property makes it a **natural and environmentally friendly indicator** in science experiments.
 
• China rose indicator is derived from the **petals of the flower** by boiling them in water.
 
• Such natural indicators are often preferred for their **non-toxic and biodegradable** nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Curry tree**__

 __
 
• **Curry tree**, scientifically known as **Murraya koenigii**, is a tropical to sub-tropical tree native to **India and Sri Lanka**.
 
• Its leaves are commonly used as a **spice in Indian cuisine** but have no known properties as a natural indicator.
 
• The tree is also valued for its **medicinal properties**, such as aiding digestion and treating infections.
 
 
 
• **Fungi**__
 __
 
• **Fungi** are a diverse group of **eukaryotic organisms** that include yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
 
• They are primarily used in **fermentation, medicine production (e.g., antibiotics like penicillin)**, and decomposition.
 
• Fungi are not known to act as natural indicators for acids and bases.
 
 
 
• **Algae**__
 
 
• **Algae** are photosynthetic organisms found in **a variety of aquatic environments.**
 
• They are primarily valued for their role in **oxygen production** and as a source of **biofuels and food supplements** such as spirulina.
 
• Algae are not used as natural indicators in acid-base experiments.

questions.question: Which treatise of Indian classical music was composed by Pandit Sharanga Deva?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sangeet Ratnakar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sangeet Ratnakar** is a highly renowned treatise on **Indian classical music and dance.**
 
• It was composed by **Pandit Sharangadeva** in the **13th century.**
 
• This work is considered a **cornerstone in the history of Indian musicology** and remains a critical text for understanding the evolution of Indian classical music.
 
• The treatise is written in **Sanskrit** and is divided into **seven chapters**, covering topics like **the science of sound, rhythm, and melody**.
 
• Sangeet Ratnakar provides detailed descriptions of **ragas, talas, and musical instruments** used during that period.
 
• It bridges the gap between the **ancient and medieval traditions** of Indian music and serves as a key reference for both **Hindustani** and **Carnatic music systems.**
 
• The treatise also includes discussions on **theatrical arts and dance forms,** making it a holistic guide to performing arts.
 
• Sangeet Ratnakar's influence extends to modern times, as it is still studied by scholars and practitioners of Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sangeet Makarand**__

 __
 
• **Sangeet Makarand** is one of the oldest treatises on Indian classical music, written by **Narada**.
 
• It provides an early classification of **ragas** and is an important work in the field of **musicology.**
 
• The treatise primarily focuses on the **technical aspects of music** but is less comprehensive compared to Sangeet Ratnakar.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Samay Saar**__
 __
 
• **Sangeet Samay Saar** is another significant text on Indian classical music, attributed to **authorical debates**.
 
• It emphasizes the **aesthetic aspects** of music, such as mood and expression, rather than technical details.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Tarang**__
 
 
• **Sangeet Tarang** is a lesser-known work in the domain of Indian classical music.
 
• It provides a brief overview of **musical compositions and performance practices.**
 
• This text is not as detailed or influential as Sangeet Ratnakar.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: The Indian reformer Jyotirao Phule was primarily critical of which social evil of the Indian society?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Caste Discrimination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jyotirao Phule**, a prominent Indian social reformer, was primarily concerned with the issue of **caste-based discrimination** in Indian society.
 
• He worked tirelessly to challenge the **Brahmanical dominance** and the oppression of lower-caste communities.
 
• Phule and his wife, **Savitribai Phule**, played a pivotal role in promoting **education for women** and **lower-caste individuals**.
 
• He founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** (Society of Truth Seekers) in 1873 to fight against caste oppression and promote social equality.
 
• Jyotirao Phule strongly criticized the **Manusmriti** and other scriptures that justified caste discrimination.
 
• He referred to the lower-caste communities as **"Shudras" and "Ati-Shudras"** and advocated for their rights and dignity.
 
• Phule’s book, **"Gulamgiri" (Slavery)**, is a scathing critique of the caste system and its entrenched injustices.
 
• He is also credited with coining the term **"Dalit"** to describe the oppressed and marginalized communities in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Poverty**__

 __
 
• Poverty refers to the state of being unable to afford basic necessities such as **food, clothing, shelter**, and healthcare.
 
• While Jyotirao Phule did acknowledge the problems caused by poverty, his primary focus remained on **caste-based inequalities**.
 
 
 
• **Sati System**__
 __
 
• The Sati system was a practice where a **widow immolated herself** on her husband’s funeral pyre.
 
• This social evil was largely addressed by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, who worked to abolish it and succeeded with the passing of the **Sati Regulation Act, 1829**.
 
 
 
• **Child Marriage**__
 
 
• Child marriage involves the **marriage of minors**, often leading to severe consequences for the health and education of young girls.
 
• Reformers like **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** and **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** worked extensively to address this issue.
tags: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India

questions.question: Which of the following states has bicameral (two houses) state legislature?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karnataka** is one of the few states in India with a **bicameral legislature**, meaning it has two houses - the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** and the **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).**
 
• The **Legislative Assembly** in Karnataka is the lower house, while the **Legislative Council** is the upper house.
 
• The system of bicameral legislatures in states is provided under **Article 169** of the **Indian Constitution**. It allows states to have a Legislative Council if the state legislature passes a resolution to that effect.
 
• The Legislative Council is a **permanent body** and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
• Karnataka's Legislative Council plays a key role in reviewing and revising legislation passed by the Legislative Assembly.
 
• Other Indian states with bicameral legislatures include **Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Goa**__

 __
 
• **Goa** has a **unicameral legislature**, meaning it has only one house - the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).**
 
• The state does not have a Legislative Council.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal**__
 __
 
• **West Bengal** also has a **unicameral legislature**, with only the **Legislative Assembly.**
 
• The state once had a Legislative Council, but it was abolished in **1969**.
 
 
 
• **Punjab**__
 
 
• **Punjab** has a **unicameral legislature** with only the **Legislative Assembly.**
 
• It does not have a Legislative Council.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT?

A) 1833 Charter Act has changed the designation for Governor-General of Bengal, renamed as Governor-General of India.

B) Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor General of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Neither A nor B**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **1833 Charter Act** was a significant legislation passed by the British Parliament aimed at reforming the administration of India.
 
• This act did **rename the Governor-General of Bengal** to the **Governor-General of India**, granting him authority over all British territories in India. However, it did not make sweeping administrative changes in his powers as implied in statement A.
 
• While the title of **Governor-General of India** was introduced, the act also centralized the power structure, bringing all provinces under the direct control of the Governor-General.
 
• **Lord William Bentinck** is widely regarded as the first Governor-General of India in terms of the title, but technically his designation was still Governor-General of Bengal under the earlier framework.
 
• The title of Governor-General of India was effectively formalized for the first time with **Lord Charles Metcalfe** serving as acting Governor-General after Bentinck, followed by Lord Auckland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Charter Act of 1833**__

 __
 
• The Charter Act of 1833 is also known as the **Government of India Act 1833**.
 
• It was the last of the series of Charter Acts passed by the British Parliament between **1793 and 1833**.
 
• The act aimed at centralizing the administration of British India by creating a unitary government under the Governor-General of India.
 
• It vested legislative power exclusively in the hands of the Governor-General in Council.
 
• The act also opened the doors for Indians to be employed in the British administration, although this was not implemented effectively.
 
 
 
• **Lord William Bentinck**__
 
 
• He served as the **Governor-General of Bengal** from **1828 to 1835**.
 
• He is known for his significant reforms in **social, economic, and educational spheres**.
 
• Bentinck is credited with abolishing the practice of **Sati** and suppressing the **Thuggee cult**.
 
• He also introduced **English as the medium of instruction** in Indian education as per Macaulay’s recommendations.
tags: India under East India Company’s Rule

questions.question: What is the term used for the line that a raider must cross to score points in Kabaddi?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Baulk line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Kabaddi**, the **Baulk line** is a crucial line that raiders must cross to score points successfully.
 
• The **Baulk line** is located at a distance of **3.75 meters** from the midline of the Kabaddi court in standard matches.
 
• The raider needs to cross this line to validate their raid attempt; failing to do so results in the raid being declared unsuccessful.
 
• Crossing the **Baulk line** helps ensure that the raider makes a genuine attempt to approach the defenders in their half of the court.
 
• Raiders must also return to their half safely after crossing the **Baulk line** to complete a successful raid.
 
• The concept of the **Baulk line** is integral to the rules of Kabaddi, ensuring fair play and strategy during the game.
 
• It is one of the most important markings on the Kabaddi court, alongside the **Bonus line** and **Centre line**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Half line**__

 __
 
• The **Half line**, also referred to as the **Centre line**, divides the Kabaddi court into two equal halves.
 
• It is the starting point for both teams and is used to separate the raiders and defenders during gameplay.
 
 
 
• **Bonus line**__
 __
 
• The **Bonus line** is located parallel to the Baulk line, at a distance of **1 meter** towards the defender’s side.
 
• If a raider crosses the **Bonus line** with one leg while the other remains in the air, they are awarded a bonus point.
 
• The bonus point can only be claimed if at least **6 defenders** are present on the court.
 
 
 
• **Centre line**__
 
 
• The **Centre line** is another term used for the **Half line**, dividing the Kabaddi court into two equal sections.
 
• It marks the starting boundary for raiders at the beginning of each raid.

questions.question:

questions.question: Which of the following folk dances is conducted during the Bwisagu Festival?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bagurumba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bwisagu Festival** is a prominent festival celebrated by the **Bodo community** of Assam, marking the arrival of the **New Year**.
 
• The **Bagurumba** is a traditional folk dance performed during this festival and is often called the **"Butterfly Dance"** because of its graceful, rhythmic movements resembling the fluttering of butterflies.
 
• It is primarily performed by **Bodo women** wearing traditional attire like the **Dokhona, Aronai, and Jwmgra**, which are vibrant and colorful.
 
• This dance symbolizes **harmony with nature**, as it reflects natural elements like birds, animals, rivers, and forests.
 
• Musical instruments such as the **Serja, Sifung (flute), and Kham (drum)** often accompany the performance, creating a lively and culturally rich atmosphere.
 
• The Bagurumba dance is not just a celebration but also a way to preserve and promote the **cultural identity** of the Bodo community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhortal**__

 __
 
• **Bhortal** is a traditional folk dance of **Assam**, performed by groups of dancers using **cymbals**.
 
• It is an energetic dance form created by the renowned Assamese artist **Narayan Chandra Goswami**.
 
• The dance is often associated with **Sattriya culture** and involves intricate rhythms and synchronized movements.
 
 
 
• **Jhumur**__
 __
 
• **Jhumur** is a traditional dance form performed by the **tea tribes** of Assam, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.
 
• This dance is characterized by **simple steps** and is performed during festivals and celebrations among the tea garden workers.
 
 
 
• **Bihu Dance**__
 
 
• The **Bihu Dance** is one of the most popular and celebrated dance forms of **Assam**, associated with the **Rongali Bihu** festival.
 
• It is performed by both men and women and is known for its **vibrant movements and traditional music**.
 
• The dance signifies **fertility, love, and joy**.

questions.question: Cyanobacteria belong to the domain of:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Producers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyanobacteria**, also known as blue-green algae, are classified as **producers** because they perform **photosynthesis** to produce their own food.
 
• They are a group of microorganisms that contain the pigment **chlorophyll-a**, which is essential for photosynthesis.
 
• Cyanobacteria can convert **sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water** into **organic compounds**, releasing **oxygen** as a byproduct.
 
• They play a crucial role in the **global carbon cycle** and are responsible for producing a significant portion of the Earth's oxygen.
 
• They are found in a wide range of environments, including **freshwater, marine systems, and terrestrial habitats**, making them ecologically versatile.
 
• Cyanobacteria are considered among the first organisms to have evolved the ability to perform **oxygenic photosynthesis**, contributing to the transformation of Earth's atmosphere billions of years ago.
 
• They are also capable of **nitrogen fixation**, converting atmospheric nitrogen into forms usable by plants, which enhances soil fertility.
 
• Examples of cyanobacteria include **Spirulina** and **Anabaena**, both of which have applications in food and agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Primary Consumers**__

 __
 
• **Primary consumers** are herbivores that feed on **producers** like plants and algae.
 
• They occupy the second trophic level in the **food chain**.
 
• Examples include **deer, rabbits, and zooplankton.**
 
 
 
• **Decomposers**__
 __
 
• **Decomposers** are organisms like fungi and bacteria that break down **dead organic matter** into simpler substances.
 
• They play a vital role in the **recycling of nutrients** in ecosystems.
 
• Examples include **mushrooms, earthworms, and certain bacteria.**
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Consumers**__
 
 
• **Tertiary consumers** are carnivores that feed on **secondary consumers**.
 
• They occupy the **top trophic levels** and are often apex predators.
 
• Examples include **eagles, lions, and sharks.**

questions.question: The oceanic trenches or the narrow depressions on the seafloor are formed by reason of:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**tectonic activity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oceanic trenches** are narrow, elongated depressions on the **seafloor**, typically occurring at depths of 7,000–11,000 meters.
 
• These trenches are formed due to the process of **subduction**, a key feature of **tectonic activity**, where one tectonic plate slides beneath another.
 
• This phenomenon occurs at **convergent plate boundaries**, where two tectonic plates move toward each other.
 
• The subducting plate bends and descends into the **mantle**, creating a trench at the surface.
 
• Examples of oceanic trenches include the **Mariana Trench** in the Pacific Ocean, which is the **deepest natural point** in the world, and the **Peru-Chile Trench**.
 
• These trenches play a vital role in the **geodynamics** of the Earth, including the recycling of the crust and the generation of earthquakes and volcanic activity.
 
• The process of subduction is also responsible for the formation of **volcanic arcs** and **earthquakes**, making trenches significant geological features.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tsunamis**__

 __
 
• **Tsunamis** are large ocean waves caused by sudden disturbances such as **underwater earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or landslides.**
 
• While they may occur near trenches due to subduction-related earthquakes, they do not directly form oceanic trenches.
 
 
 
• **Thermohaline circulation**__
 __
 
• **Thermohaline circulation** refers to the global movement of ocean water driven by differences in **temperature** and **salinity**.
 
• This process is critical for regulating the **Earth's climate** but has no role in trench formation.
 
 
 
• **Tidal currents**__
 
 
• **Tidal currents** are horizontal movements of water caused by the **gravitational pull** of the moon and the sun.
 
• They are responsible for coastal phenomena but have no connection to the formation of trenches.

questions.question: In the number 0.002609, the number of significant figures is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Significant figures** are the digits in a number that carry meaningful contributions to its measurement precision. This includes all non-zero digits, any zeros between significant digits, and any trailing zeros in a decimal number.
 
• In the number **0.002609**:
 
 
• The leading zeros (**0.00**) are not counted as significant figures because they only serve to position the decimal point.
 
• The digits **2, 6, 0, and 9** are all significant because they contribute to the precision of the number.
 
 
 
• Thus, the number of significant figures in **0.002609** is **four**.
 
• This concept is crucial in fields like **science, engineering, and statistics**, where precision in numerical values is essential.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Significant Figures Rules:**

 
 
• All **non-zero digits** are significant.
 
• Zeros between non-zero digits are significant.
 
• Leading zeros (zeros before the first non-zero digit) are not significant.
 
• Trailing zeros in a decimal number are significant.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Significant figures are widely used in **scientific measurements** to ensure that results are reported with appropriate precision.
 
• They are essential in fields like **chemistry, physics, and engineering**, where precision directly impacts the accuracy of experiments and calculations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a salient feature of Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: There is clear difference between Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties.
Fundamental Duties are both civic and moral in nature.
They are enforceable by law and can be challenged in court.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**They are enforceable by law and can be challenged in court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties** in the Indian Constitution are listed in **Article 51A** under Part IV-A.
 
• These duties were added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, inspired by the Constitution of the former **USSR**.
 
• Fundamental Duties are **non-justiciable**, meaning their implementation cannot be enforced by courts.
 
• They are designed to promote a sense of **civic responsibility** and **moral obligation** among citizens.
 
• The statement "They are enforceable by law and can be challenged in court" is incorrect because Fundamental Duties do not have legal backing to compel their adherence or challenge their violation in a court of law.
 
• Though non-justiciable, these duties serve as a reminder to citizens to uphold **national values** and act as a guiding principle for the **legislature** in framing laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It is non-justiciable.**__

 __
 
• The Fundamental Duties are explicitly **non-justiciable**, meaning their violation cannot be challenged in a court of law.
 
• This characteristic distinguishes them from **Fundamental Rights**, which are enforceable in courts.
 
 
 
• **There is clear difference between Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties.**__
 __
 
• **Fundamental Rights** focus on individual freedoms and liberties, whereas **Fundamental Duties** emphasize responsibilities and obligations towards the nation.
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable in a court of law, while Duties are non-enforceable.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties are both civic and moral in nature.**__
 
 
• These duties reflect a blend of **civic responsibilities** such as respecting the Constitution and **moral obligations** like protecting the environment.
 
• They aim to instill a sense of **national pride** and moral consciousness among citizens.

questions.question: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), what is the percentage of the total population who are multidimensionally poor (Headcount Ratio) in Bihar state?

__
 
• The **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2023** is a significant report that measures poverty using a multidimensional approach, considering various factors such as education, health, and living standards.
 
• According to this report, the **Headcount Ratio** represents the proportion of the population that is classified as multidimensionally poor.
 
• For the state of **Bihar**, the Headcount Ratio is **0.3376**, meaning approximately 33.76% of the population in Bihar is multidimensionally poor.
 
• Bihar is one of the states in India with the highest levels of poverty, as highlighted in the report, despite recent efforts to improve socio-economic conditions.
 
• The **MPI** is a globally recognized measure developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)**.
 
• This index highlights the need for targeted interventions to address poverty in Bihar, focusing on improving access to education, healthcare, and basic amenities.
 
• The multidimensional approach provides a more comprehensive understanding of poverty compared to traditional income-based measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the National Multidimensional Poverty Index**__

 __
 
• The MPI is based on three main dimensions: **health, education, and standard of living**.
 
• Each dimension is further broken down into indicators such as **child mortality, years of schooling, nutrition, sanitation, and access to clean drinking water**.
 
• It helps policymakers prioritize and design interventions targeting specific dimensions of poverty.
 
• The MPI aligns with the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 1: **No Poverty**.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Incorrect Options**__
 
 
• The other options such as **0.3612, 0.4598, and 0.4054** are incorrect as they do not match the officially reported Headcount Ratio for Bihar in the **2023 National MPI Report**.
 
• The correct value, **0.3376**, has been derived from comprehensive data analysis conducted by the report's authors.

questions.question: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs?

options.text: Social mobilisation, economic development, and education
Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building of the poor

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building of the poor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Social mobilisation** refers to the process of bringing together individuals, groups, or communities to collectively work towards a common goal. In the context of **SAPAP** (South Asia Poverty Alleviation Program) for **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**, it focuses on empowering the poor by uniting them to take collective action for their development and rights.
 
• **Capital formation** is a critical component that emphasizes building financial resources for SHGs. Through savings, access to credit, and efficient utilization of funds, SHGs are able to invest in income-generating activities, thereby contributing to economic empowerment.
 
• **Capacity building of the poor** involves enhancing the skills, knowledge, and abilities of individuals in SHGs. This is accomplished through training, education, and workshops, enabling members to better manage their groups, finances, and livelihood projects.
 
• The integration of these three components—**social mobilisation**, **capital formation**, and **capacity building**—creates a holistic empowerment model that aims to reduce poverty and improve the socio-economic status of vulnerable populations.
 
• These components together form the foundation of the **SAPAP framework**, which has been instrumental in addressing poverty and enhancing **self-reliance** among marginalized communities in **South Asia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Social mobilisation, economic development, and education**__

 __
 
• While **economic development** and **education** are important for overall societal progress, they do not specifically align with the core framework of **SAPAP**. The focus of SAPAP is on poverty alleviation through grassroots initiatives like capacity building and financial support.
 
• **Education** is often a long-term strategy, whereas SAPAP emphasizes immediate empowerment through SHG-driven approaches.
 
 
 
• **Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication**__
 __
 
• This option partially overlaps with the correct answer as it mentions **capital formation**. However, **poverty eradication** is an outcome rather than a component of the empowerment model.
 
• **Collective empowerment** is a broader concept that encompasses various social and economic aspects but does not specifically address the structured approach outlined by SAPAP.
 
 
 
• **Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance**__
 
 
• **Public resource allocation** focuses on government or institutional distribution of resources, which is not a key component of the SAPAP empowerment model.
 
• Although **microfinance** plays a role in SHG operations, it is a tool rather than a core element of the empowerment model.

questions.question: Harappa, one of the sites of the Harappan culture, was found in which of the following states of pre-independent India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harappa** was one of the most significant cities of the **Indus Valley Civilization** and is an archaeological site situated in present-day **Pakistan's Punjab province**.
 
• During **pre-independent India**, this region was part of the larger Punjab province under British rule.
 
• Harappa was discovered in the early **1920s** by **Daya Ram Sahni** under the supervision of the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).**
 
• The site is known for its advanced urban planning, including features like a sophisticated **drainage system**, well-structured houses, and a unique grid-based street layout.
 
• Artifacts such as **seals, pottery, beads, and tools** have been uncovered, offering insights into the culture, trade, and daily life of the Harappan people.
 
• The city is believed to have been a major center of trade and administration during the peak of the **Indus Valley Civilization (2600–1900 BCE).**
 
• The name "Harappan Civilization" is derived from this site, as it was the first city of the civilization to be excavated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Balochistan**__

 __
 
• **Balochistan** is a province in present-day Pakistan, but it was not the location of Harappa. However, another significant Indus Valley site, **Mehrgarh**, is located in Balochistan.
 
• **Mehrgarh** is one of the earliest known agricultural settlements (7000 BCE) and predates the Harappan Civilization.
 
 
 
• **Sindh**__
 __
 
• **Sindh** is a province in present-day Pakistan and was part of pre-independent India's Bombay Presidency.
 
• It is home to another major Indus Valley site, **Mohenjo-daro**, known for its advanced urban features and iconic "Great Bath."
 
 
 
• **United Province**__
 
 
• The **United Province** (modern-day Uttar Pradesh) in pre-independent India was not associated with the Harappan sites.
 
• This region was historically significant for other cultures and civilizations, such as the **Vedic Period** and the **Mauryan Empire**, but not the Indus Valley Civilization.
